name: Question 3
problem:
Given the matrix 
$G=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -5 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(G).$
worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(G),$ we reduce the matrix $G$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}G & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -5 \\ 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${g}_{1}$ and ${g}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(G)$ is ${{g}_{1},{g}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Question 3
?

Given the matrix G=[00−5520000]. Find a basis B of Col(G).

a
B={[−500]}
b
B={[050],[−500]}
c
B={[050],[020]}
d
B={[050]}
e
B={[050],[020],[−500]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In order to find a basis of Col(G), we reduce the matrix G to row echelon form:

G=[00−5520000]R1↔R2∼[52000−5000]

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the 1st and 3rd columns are pivot columns, while the 2nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the original matrix, not from the reduced one.

The 1st and 3rd columns from the original matrix are g1 and g3. So, a basis of Col(G) is {g1,g3}, that is to say,

B={[050],[−500]}.
